title: We’re Sharing October Prime Day Discounts Live—Follow Along Here
author: WIRED
text: It’s the last day of Amazon Prime Day. All mediocre-to-good things must come to an end, and with caffeine in our brains and years of expertise in our hearts, we're here once again to sift through the pile of nonsense to find the deals on gear that'll be great far past the initial hit of dopamine when it arrives at your door.Our fabulous WIRED reviewers will be popping into this live blog throughout the day to yap about the stuff they’re buying and the bargains we think you should know about. We’ll also regularly be updating our Absolute Best Prime Day Deals.Louryn Strampe3 minutes agoLineGet A Head Start on Your Fitness Goals with These Prime Day PicksAmazon Prime DayThe Best Prime Day Fitness Deals, From Smartwatches to Massage GunsBy Boutayna Chokrane Read MoreReviewer Boutayna Chokrane is always on her way to Pilates or yoga when the girls catch up via FaceTime, seemingly no matter the time of day. I personally have learned a thing or twelve from her regarding personal fitness, and she's rounded up a whole list of deals worth checking out that can probably help you, too. From recovery tools to treadmills to trackers, you don't need to wait until the new year arrives to start reaching toward your fitness goals.Louryn Strampe18 minutes agoLineThe Iconic Razer Kitty Kraken Headset Is Down to Its Second-Best PriceRazerKraken Kitty V3 Pro$180 $150 (17% off) Amazon$180 Razer$180 $150 (17% off) Best BuyI'm sorry to say that at one point this year, before I got to test it, this headset fell to $100. But I've been checking it out for a few days, I love it very much, and every color is at least somewhat discounted thanks to Prime Day. The Razer Kraken Kitty V3 Pro has the iconic cat ears attached, plus RGB lights throughout the ears and earcups for slick reactive rainbows. I love the retractable mic and the sound quality, and so far it's been very comfortable. Add on three modes of connectivity and I'm still blogging about it since it will be a pick in an upcoming guide refresh. It's cute and nobody can stop me! I can't confirm nor deny that the ears add any speed to your gamer reflexes, but if you'd like to test the theory for yourself, do it at a slight discount.Harry Rabinowitz40 minutes agoLineI Call Mom More Because Of These EarbudsPhotograph: Harry RabinowitzSoundcore by AnkerLiberty 5 Pro$170 $136 (20% off) Amazon$170 $145 (15% off) Best Buy$170 SoundcoreI have aging parents who are losing their hearing, and I like to mumble. That’s a bad combination for phone calls, especially in a loud place like New York City. The Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro solved this problem. I sound amazingly clear and loud on all my phone calls, no matter where I am. Firetrucks, highway overpasses, loud cafes, no background noise stopped me from having clear calls where I never had to repeat myself. I recommend these earbuds even at full price—this is the first time they’ve been on sale, and 20 percent off feels like icing on the cake.Louryn Strampean hour agoLineThe Best Art TV, Now At Its Lowest PricePhotograph: John BrandonSamsungThe Frame Pro (2026)$1,798 $1,597 (11% off) AmazonArt TVs are for what I'd call a “specific audience." Some of us aren't bothered by the black box on our wall or entertainment center when the set isn't on. Some of us cannot stand it. This is the best price we've ever seen for Samsung's The Frame Pro, which is our top art TV overall. It displays gorgeous art images that look great thanks to the high contrast and anti-glare coating. It's a bummer that some of the art is locked behind a monthly subscription, but we think this model is hard to beat for folks in the market for this specific and luxurious item. Personally, I'm OK with the Roku Backdrops that shuffle, but my TV was also $200 and is not at all the centerpiece of my home. Should I get an art TV? Much to consider… Nena Farrell an hour agoLineGet My Next Robot Vacuum Pick While It’s On SaleRoborockSaros 20$1,600 $1,180 (26% off) Amazon$1,600 $1,195 (25% off) RoborockI’m constantly testing robot vacuums, but sometimes, they all blur together, especially when some brands are pumping out constant new models. Roborock is guilty of that, with so many new models out this year we’ve barely been able to review them all. But the latest one I’m testing has actually left me happy and impressed with its work around my house.While most robot vacuums don’t really seem to see spills like they say they will, the Roborock Saros 20 did see the cherry stain spill I put in its path and meticulously cleaned it. I also really liked that it went back to the dock afterwards to wash its pad, so there was no worry about the cherry juice being spread across more of my floors (which has happened with less intelligent vacuums!) It’ll be coming to my guide to robot vacuums soon as a new pick.Louryn Strampe2 hours agoLineThe Best-Looking Bottle Washer Is Down to Its Best PricePhotograph: Nicole KinningMomcozyKleanPal Pro Baby Bottle Washer and Sterilizer$300 $225 (25% off) Amazon$300 Walmart$300 MomcozyThere's a lot of nonsense marketed to new parents, but bottle washers actually provide a necessary service. You could run your dishwasher 24 hours per day, or you could pick up this countertop bottle washer and sanitizer. It has a few different cleaning modes, including a quick 19-minute wash cycle that might come to the rescue if your hands are full. Your newborn does not need shoes. But you, or your expecting friends, do need to keep them fed. This price beats the previous lowest we've seen.Kat Merck2 hours agoLineA Trip to the Mechanic? Not in This EconomyCourtesy of AmazonAncelAD310 Classic Enhanced Universal OBD II Scanner$40 $30 (25% off) AmazonDo you have an older vehicle, or a vehicle of dubious reliability? It would probably make sense for you to have an OBD II reader. If your check engine light comes on, you’ll be able to interpret the code that caused it and determine whether it’s A) something you can ignore until you have the time or money to get it fixed, B) something you can fix yourself, or C) something severe enough to stop driving the car. Or, if there’s an entire library’s worth of codes, give up and sell the car to someone on the side of the road for $2,500, as I did once with an old Camaro I was tired of fixing. Anyway, I bought this OBDII reader a few months ago for my 2nd gen Tundra (just in case!) and have been quite impressed with the features and the quality for the price—which is even better right now at 25 percent off.Les Shu3 hours agoLineA Waterproof Sound System for My BathroomPhotograph: Chris HaslamAnkerSoundcore 2$45 $28 (38% off) AmazonMy colleague, Harry Rabinowitz, who oversees WIRED’s audio coverage, recommended this budget option when I inquired about a speaker for my bathroom. I needed something that could produce good-quality sound for music and podcasts, yet could withstand the humidity or (God forbid) accidental drops into water. I also like that it’s portable, so I don’t need to sacrifice an outlet to power it, and I can take it with me on the road. It’s normally affordable, but the sale makes it even more attractive.Louryn Strampe3 hours agoLineHere's A Fresh Roundup of Phone Accessory Deals!Amazon Prime DayStock Up on the Best Prime Day Deals on Phone AccessoriesBy Les ShuRead MoreWhether it be a portable charger, a MagSafe wallet, a cable or controller, or something else, we have a new roundup of the best phone accessory deals. There's even a wall adapter so you can have a backup if your housemates are constantly stealing yours.Harry Rabinowitz3 hours agoLineBose Headphones for 53 Percent Off?!Courtesy of AmazonBoseQuietComfort Headphones (1st Gen)$359 $169 (53% off) Amazon$359 $169 (53% off) Best Buy$359 $169 (53% off) WalmartBose QuietComfort Headphones are 53 percent off right now—that’s $190 off sticker price, and about $100 less than how much they usually go for. They are classic travel headphones for a reason, with excellent automated noise-canceling, a super comfortable and light fit, and a compact design that folds into a neat travel case. And this might be the last hurrah for these headphones, since Bose recently launched the QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), hence the super low price. Different colors are on sale at different retailers.Louryn Strampe3 hours agoLineMy Favorite Bedroom Light Is Down to Its Lowest PriceGoveeBasic Floor Lamp$100 $60 (40% off) AmazonI bought this lamp in June, and got another for my friend. I like it a lot, especially for the price! Govee makes good gear in general, and this lamp is simple, but effective at creating ambiance and a vibe. I put it in the corner and use it to set the mood for gaming, reading, movie night with my lover, and waking up in the morning. The app is pretty easy to use. I do wish the cord was a little longer, but that's mostly a fault of my vintage home outlet locations and not necessarily the lamp itself. This price is a match of the best we've tracked.Louryn Strampe4 hours agoLineI Love This Cooler And Somehow It's Still On SalePhotograph: Louryn StrampeYetiRoadie 32$375 $285 (24% off) Amazon$375 Yeti$375 REIAs the lead cooler tester, I have a lot of these bad boys in my house. The Yeti Roadie 32 is the one I take with me on all my trips, from beach days to camping festivals. It's pretty easy to navigate around, though the handle is on the short side, and it keeps ice for days and items cold for even longer. I also like the lid latches and the drain mechanism. These don't go on sale often, so even though it's out of season, I'd still recommend considering it if you want a really efficient cooler that isn't monstrously large.You can find even more Yeti Prime Day deals here.Simon Hill4 hours agoLineThis Deal’s No Drip, But Can Detect OnePhotograph: Simon HillX-SenseWi-Fi Water Leak Detector$63 $50 (21% off) Amazon (4-Pack)$16 $11 (31% off) Amazon (Add-On)Okay, okay, I know it’s not exciting. You’re not shopping for something as practical as a water leak detector, much less a three-pack with a smart hub to alert you to drips, dribbles, and leaks all over your home. So, it’s one of the best water leak detectors, capable of detecting pools of water as shallow as 0.4 mm. So what? You’d much rather buy something sexy. Some shiny, seductive new toy you can show off to your friends. Who needs an ear-splitting 110-decibel alarm or reliable and swift push notifications on their phone when things get wet?Besides, I’m sure your insurance will pay for that leaky pipe, the bath your kid left running, and the possessed washing machine in your basement, right? Yeah, sure they will. Don’t worry. Water leak detectors are for boring losers who like to live in dry houses and avoid crippling water damage repairs. Go buy something shiny instead.Kat Merck4 hours agoLineAs I sit here eating my breakfast at 6 am on the West Coast, which is oatmeal with fruits and nuts because I'm middle aged, something has occurred to me: Do people really like dried papaya? You don’t typically see it readily available by itself in snack bags, like you do with dried mango, and there’s just something off about the taste, like an elderly slice of hotel-buffet melon that fell on the floor for a few hours and ended up back on the table.Photograph: Kat MerckAs you can see, there is a gigantic random chunk of it in my oatmeal right now, courtesy of the trail mix I bought last week, and it’s bumming me out. If you too prefer a papaya-free trail mix, Power Up Mega Omega is the kind I usually buy.Courtesy of AmazonPower UpMega Omega Trail Mix$7 $6 (14% off) AmazonThe sale isn’t one to write home about, but this is a much better price than I paid for it last at the grocery store. Note that kids tend not to like this trail mix due to the dearth of M&Ms and cashews, and some (like mine) may refuse to eat at all on a hike or trip if this is the only option presented to them. So make sure you, presumably an anti-papaya adult, are buying it for yourself.Louryn Strampe3 hours agoLineDon't worry, Kat, I'll eat all of your dried papaya. Please send in the mail posthaste.Louryn Strampe5 hours agoLineGood Morning Shoppers, It's Caffeine TimeWelcome to day two of the Amazon Prime Day Big Deal Days Super Huge Sale Extravaganza. Myself and my fellow Reviews team members are here once again to find the discounts worth your hard-earned money.Photograph: Pete CottellCelsiusFunctional Essential Energy Drink, Sparkling Orange (12-pack)$24 $19 (21% off) AmazonEnergy drink opinions vary greatly, but most of us on the team like Celsius for its bright, not-too-sweet taste and eye-watering caffeine content. It's on sale in many flavors.StanleyThe Quencher H2.0 Flowstate 40-Ounce Tumbler$40 $22 (45% off) Shop$45 $30 (33% off) Amazon$45 $34 (24% off) StanleyAnd if you want to do the “right” thing you can start out by hydrating first. I love this tumbler, which I bought during Prime Day earlier this year or perhaps four or six years ago. Prime Day is infinite. Let us go forth into another. Nena Farrell 17 hours agoLineThat’s a Wrap on Day One's DealsThe first half of Prime Day is coming for an end, but we'll be back tomorrow with more great deals we've spotted and are even shopping ourselves. If you're hungry for more deals while you wait, check out our guide to the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals to see what's worth buying.Kat Merck17 hours agoLineEveryone Needs to Hear About This Dish Soap I BoughtCourtesy of AmazonDawnPowerwash Spray Dish Soap$18 $12 (33% off) AmazonI, for one, always enjoy posts about what people actually bought for Prime Day, so I present to you the one thing I myself have bought: dish detergent. Apparently spray-on dish detergent has been around since 2020, but I just became aware of Dawn Powerwash this summer when I saw it on an endcap at the grocery store and bought it on a whim (typically I do grocery pickup to curb my impulse shopping, but this time it paid off!). I am not ashamed to admit that dish spray in a bottle has changed my life. It’s not only a no-mess, only-spray-what-you-need solution for dishes, but you can use it to clean all sorts of things, from clothes to your car. One bottle of Powerwash is $5 at most grocery stores, so not only are you saving $2 a bottle with this deal, it’s being delivered right to your house, so you won’t go to the store and impulse-buy other things. Win-win! Nena Farrell 17 hours agoLineMy Best Hair Ever Is Thanks To This HatPhotograph: Nena FarrellHigherDoseRed Light Hat$449 $359 (20% off) Amazon$449 HigherDoseIt might look like a baseball cap, but this red light hat unlocked my best hair ever. I'm pregnant now and everyone has compliments for my hair, but I know the real source of this was my red light hat I religiously wore at the end of last year into this year. The HigherDose Red Light Hat transformed my hair from patchy into shiny and healthy, and my sensitive scalp stopped breaking out into itchy sections. Red light is currently not recommended for me as a pregnant woman, but I can't wait to rock this hat again next year to help me escape the postpartum uglies. Nena Farrell 18 hours agoLineChat, Should I Get My Husband a Smart Bird Feeder for Christmas?I beg of you: nobody send this blog to my husband. He always manages to surprise me on Christmas morning with something thoughtful, and a smart bird feeder has been something I'm plotting to get him.Photograph: Kat MerckBirdfyBamboo Feeder With Camera$230 $184 (20% off) Amazon (no AI ID, guard)$300 $180 (40% off) Amazon (AI ID, no guard)$300 $204 (32% off) Amazon (AI ID, guard)My husband and son love going on evening walks to see the animals and birds, but soon it'll get dark too early for him to enjoy them after a work day. The solution? A smart bird feeder that will record video they can enjoy together after dinner, seeing what birds came to visit. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck says this is the best-looking smart bird feeder she's tested, and it's got a nice discount for Prime Day. Nena Farrell 18 hours agoLineOf All Things, a Multicooker Is Top of My Prime Day WishlistCrock-PotMultiMeal Multicooker and Programmable Slow Cooker$190 $150 (21% off) Crate & Barrel$170 $145 (15% off) TargetI have a problem. I'm obsessed with this slow cooker.I already have a regular slow cooker and a multicooker at home, so I don't need this one. But I can't stop thinking about it. All I can think about is how fun it would be to have two things cooking side by side for holiday events, like two kinds of hot chocolate or mashed potatoes in one half with meatballs and gravy on the other. The pairings are endless, and I want it for every holiday party this season. Will I pull the trigger? I'll report back after Prime Day ends if I added it to my purchases.
